- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. - update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". - fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

Notes on how these break down:

- `store/driver.go:29-32` is the interface contract (`CreateMemo`/`ListMemos` take/return `*Memo`), so all three drivers under `store/db/` must change together — they do the column scanning and INSERT/UPDATE field lists.
- If a *field* is added/renamed (not just a method), the SQL schema is coupled too: `store/migration/{sqlite,postgres,mysql}/LATEST.sql` plus a new versioned migration directory, and `store/seed/sqlite/01__dump.sql`.
- The heaviest consumer is `server/router/api/v1/` — `memo_service_converter.go` is the store→proto boundary and is where most field-level breakage will surface.
- `server/router/api/v1/user_service_stats.go`, `memo_service_comments.go`, `attachment_service.go`, `fileserver/fileserver.go`, and `frontend/frontend.go` don't name `store.Memo` explicitly — they get it back from `ListMemos`/`GetMemo` and read fields (`memo.Visibility`, `memo.CreatorID`, `memo.CreatedTs`, …), so a grep for the literal type name misses them.
- `store/db/{sqlite,postgres,mysql}/user_delete.go` reads `memo.ID`/`memo.UID` but on a local `deleteUserMemoRef` struct, not `store.Memo` — not affected.
